business_scope.primary_industry_name: Real Estate Property Management and Rental Screening Cloud

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union — free movement of capital, freedom of establishment and EU company law harmonization

Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) investment protection agreements with non-EU states, including the BLEU–China Agreement on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 4 June 1984, as applicable)

Luxembourg Double Tax Convention network, including treaties with Germany, France, Netherlands, Belgium, United Kingdom, United States, Switzerland, United Arab Emirates, Singapore, Hong Kong SAR, and China
EU Association and cooperation agreements with third countries, where applicable to the ultimate investor chain

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO Law), as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 22 July 2019 concerning the practical operation of the UBO Register; amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS Law); CSSF Regulation No 12-02 for professionals of the financial sector; CSSF Circulars and guidance on AML/CFT risk-based approach.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of each individual shareholder's passport or national identity card
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent authority in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles, and registry excerpt for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certificate of registered office for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry or authorized filing agent in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled power of attorney, where a local resident manager or corporate service provider acts on behalf of the founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or certified confirmation of source of funds from the paying bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization if required by the receiving Luxembourg notary or registry; otherwise original on bank letterhead

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under the Luxembourg AML/CFT Law. Each direct shareholder, indirect shareholder pursuing a 25% or more ownership or control right, and every beneficial owner must be screened against EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council designations, Luxembourg national terror-financing lists, OFAC listings to the extent applicable to the financing bank or payment chain, and other international sanctions databases. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) — both foreign and domestic — must be identified through reliable electronic and manual screening; if detected, enhanced due diligence applies, including written source of wealth and source of funds declarations, senior management approval, enhanced monitoring of the business relationship, and higher-frequency update of the UBO register profile.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic portal at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the working language of the RCS; statutory filings may be prepared in French or German. The legal form must be expressed as 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or its usual abbreviation 'SARL'. Non-Latin script corporate names of constituents must be transliterated and, where required, certified-translated into French or German. The proposed company name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS-validated name and must contain no misleading or unlawful element. The full corporate name, including the legal form suffix, must be set out in the notarial deed of incorporation exactly as reserved by the negative certificate.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS refuses the proposed name, the applicant may file an administrative complaint with the Ministry of Justice through the RCS supervisory hierarchy within one month of the refusal notification. An independent action may be brought before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg for annulment of the refusal. In practice, the simplest and most pragmatic remedy is to submit a new name for a fresh negative certificate, while preserving the right to appeal the initial refusal if the name is commercially essential. The negative certificate or name reservation must be used before expiry; after expiration, a new application for a negative certificate must be filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual office address is not acceptable as the registered office of a Luxembourg SARL. The registered office must be a physical address in Luxembourg where the company's corporate records can be inspected, legal process can be received, and general administration can be carried out. A serviced office, business center or registered office rental from a regulated corporate service provider may be acceptable if supported by a genuine service agreement and the location is not merely a mail-forwarding facility. For a PropTech SaaS platform, a serviced office with substantive managed infrastructure is acceptable for incorporation, but the company should maintain local business substance appropriate to its activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a standard low-risk PropTech SaaS SARL. Unannounced physical on-site inspections by the RCS, the tax administration and, in cross-border contexts, the Luxembourg social security authorities, are not routine but can occur where substance red flags arise, such as all corporate bodies residing abroad, no local employees, a shared mail-drop address, absent accounting records, or recurring losses. For an ordinary SARL with one or two employees and a registered serviced office, the estimated annual probability of an unannounced inspection is below 5%; if substance indicators are weak, the probability rises to 15% or higher in a given fiscal year.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Negative name clearance certificate (certificat du négatif) at the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory fee tariff for a negative name certificate; approximately EUR 15 in official fees, converted at 1.08 USD/EUR.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization of five corporate and identity documents for foreign founding parties
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille office, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or consulate of the document's country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official per-document fee variants from USD 25 to USD 65; aggregate estimate for five documents at prevailing public tariffs.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of apostilled foreign corporate documents, passports and powers of attorney into French
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn/en-court certified translator in Luxembourg or the shareholder's jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for certified translation: approximately USD 65 per page, estimated at five pages.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation of the SARL, including notary's verification of assets, articles of association drafting, and UBO formalities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff for an SARL with share capital of EUR 12,000; minimum notarial duty approximately EUR 1,300 plus VAT, with additional official disbursements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration and legal publication in the Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official filing and publication tariff; includes simultaneous registration with the RCS and announcement in the Luxembourg official electronic gazette.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register initial filing (no official fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: The initial UBO declaration under the UBO Law of 13 January 2019 is filed without an official filing fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Proof of registered office: serviced office agreement and notarized landlord consent for corporate use
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Serviced office provider and Luxembourg notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Provider administration fee for initial registration documentation plus notarial/confirmed signature fees; monthly office rental excluded from pre-incorporation budget.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External counsel pre-incorporation due diligence: UBO report, PEP/sanctions screening, and registration compliance memorandum
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional fee benchmark for a standard SARL incorporation: USD 250 to USD 400 per hour, estimated at three to four hours.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; SARL provisions set out in Articles 710-1 to 710-14 of the said Law.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized articles of incorporation (acte constitutif / statuts coordonnés) plus the application for registration with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum statutory capital for a SARL is EUR 12,000. All quotas must be fully subscribed and at least 25% of each quota must be paid up at incorporation. The unpaid balance must be paid within five years. Capital must be deposited on a blocked escrow bank account in Luxembourg and can be released only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF MANAGERS OF [•] SARL, held on [•], at the registered office in Luxembourg. After noting the share subscriptions and the capital-blocking certificate obtained from [Bank], the board unanimously resolved: (1) that all subscribed quotas are accepted, allotted and deemed fully paid to the extent required by law; (2) that the registered office is established at [street address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, as set out in the articles; (3) that [•] is appointed sole gérant, with authority to act singly, and that any legal domiciliation or power-of-attorney formalities are approved; (4) that the blocked registry capital be released and applied in accordance with statute; (5) that the tax, VAT and social security registrations be filed without delay; and (6) that bank mandates and signatory cards be executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS, online via MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search in the RCS index. File a name reservation request through MyGuichet.lu, indicating the proposed SARL name, its corporate object, and the legal form. The registry issues a certificate of availability confirming that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing Luxembourg undertaking.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on similarity grounds, submit two alternative names and, if necessary, furnish a notarial explanation or amend the name by written shareholder resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow Deposit and Blocking Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) under CSSF supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate formation account in the name of the SARL en formation. Transfer the required minimum capital from the shareholders' own bank accounts. The bank will issue a capital-blocking certificate confirming the deposit and that the funds remain frozen until the RCS registration is completed.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all subscribers and proposed managers
Source of funds and anti-money laundering declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank questions the source of funds, provide bank statements, salary slips, or third-party confirmatory letters establishing lawful origin; amend declarations and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (notaire), member of the Chambre des Notaires
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the notarial deed in French before a Luxembourg notary. The notary verifies the legality of the articles, the capital-blocking certificate, and the identity and capacity of the subscribers. The parties and the notary sign the deed; certified copies are then produced for registration.
required_dossiers: List of subscribers with passport copies
Evidence of the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal defects, amend the draft articles and re-notarize; if a subscriber lacks capacity, obtain a notarized proxy or certified power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized articles of incorporation with the RCS together with the application for registration, the beneficial owner information, and a certified copy of the capital-blocking certificate. The registry examines compliance with the Law of 10 August 1915 and then enters the company in the commercial register, issuing a Luxembourg RCS registration number.
required_dossiers: Application for RCS registration signed by a manager
Consent of the registered office occupier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, correct the filing within fifteen days; appeal an unjustified refusal before the competent court under RCS procedural rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal Publication in the Electronic Gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal Publications Service of the Luxembourg Business Registers – RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, submit the registration extract and appended statutory documents to the official electronic legal journal RESA. The publication provides legal notice to third parties and completes the statutory publicity requirement.
required_dossiers: Names and signatures of the appointed managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is rejected for incomplete information, the registry office will notify the company; complete the missing fields within ten working days to perfect legal effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement et des Domaines; Administration des Contributions Directes; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply electronically through MyGuichet.lu for a Luxembourg VAT number and corporate income tax reference number. Simultaneously register the company as an employer with the CCSS for social security purposes, and complete any required registrations for the managing director and staff.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of shareholders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or VAT registration is delayed beyond the SLA, file a follow-up with the ACD supported by the RCS extract; late registration penalties may be mitigated by promptly regularizing the status.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Industry, New Technologies and Economic Development (Direction Générale de l'Industrie)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit required for ISIC 6201 (software publishing and SaaS services); no industrial establishment authorization is necessary for pure office-based PropTech activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement – Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Non-industrial office activity under the EIA category system; no full EIA report required because the ISIC 6201 software and SaaS service does not trigger the thresholds of the Luxembourg environmental impact assessment legislation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with municipal sewerage regulations; only domestic wastewater is generated. No significant VOC or industrial emissions arise. Waste handling must comply with the Luxembourg Waste Law of 21 March 2017 and EU Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006, with disposal through an approved waste operator.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification must be obtained from the Luxembourg Fire and Rescue Service (Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours), covering evacuation routes, smoke detection, and alarm systems. Structural load clearance from the building owner is required for office occupancy. Occupational workplace clearance must be provided by the Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) covering electrical safety, ventilation, sanitary facilities, and general worker health and safety conditions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) for direct taxes; Registration, Estates and VAT Administration (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, AEDV) for VAT; principal portal: guichet.lu; online VAT filing portal: eTVA.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SARL, the company is registered ex officio upon incorporation. A foreign entity without a Luxembourg establishment must apply for a VAT identification number to the AEDV using Form 563 (available via MyGuichet.lu) and, unless exempt under special measures, must appoint a Luxembourg-established VAT representative. Direct tax registration for a permanent establishment is done through the ACD by filing the annual corporate tax return and registering on the eCDF platform; the company obtains a national business number (numéro de registre) from the Luxembourg Business Registers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg; a SARL is mandatorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax. Available elections include the option to form a single taxable person for VAT purposes (VAT grouping under Article 60 Loi TVA), optional tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Article 164 bis LIR for qualifying resident companies, and certain hybrid mismatch alignment elections required by the European Union Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT, Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (small business exemption under Article 57 Loi TVA); exemption does not apply to certain digital/electronic services; non-established taxable persons supplying digital services or goods from abroad are obliged to register from the first euro of Luxembourg taxable turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API reporting, or digital stamping mandate applies for B2B invoicing. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for B2G supplies through Peppol when responding to public tenders. All VAT returns and recapitulative statements (EC Sales Lists) must be filed electronically via the eTVA portal. Invoices must comply with Directive 2006/112/EC authenticity, integrity, and content requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods outside the European Union is zero-rated where the supplier retains commercial and customs evidence proving that the goods left Luxembourg/EU territory within the prescribed timeframe (generally within 90 days of dispatment). Qualifying intra-EU dispatches to a taxable person are likewise zero-rated when the customer's valid EU VAT number is stated. Offshore digital and SaaS services supplied to a foreign recipient outside the EU fall outside the Luxembourg VAT scope (no VAT), provided the place of supply rules are met; zero-rating also applies to certain international services relating to intellectual property or real estate located abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EX-A/SAD customs declaration in the exporting member state)
Bill of Lading (or equivalent transport document, e.g., CMR or air waybill)
Inward Remittance Certificate (proof of payment in foreign currency received from the non-EU buyer)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax authorities scrutinize documentary evidence for zero-rated exports; if substantiation is inadequate or false, a VAT assessment on the export transaction is issued for the standard rate, with default interest from the due date of the VAT return, administrative fines (up to 10% of the tax amount for non-fraudulent errors, and higher penalties for bad faith), and criminal sanctions for deliberate fraud. Retroactive clawbacks may reach all undeclared VAT plus interest, and liability can extend to the responsible directors and the appointed VAT representative.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), which jointly administer Luxembourg's monetary, financial-stability, and banking-prudential compliance framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg, as an EU Member State within the euro area, maintains unrestricted currency convertibility. Both current-account items (dividends, interest, royalties, service fees) and capital-account operations (equity injections, intercompany financing, M&A transactions) are free from exchange-control approvals, quantitative limits, or forced conversion. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is legally unrestricted; any tax leakage is limited to withholding taxes under domestic law and applicable tax treaties, not FX controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender obligations for export proceeds, receivables, or SaaS subscription revenues in Luxembourg. Exporters are free to retain foreign currency offshore or onshore without mandatory conversion into euros. The BCL imposes only statistical reporting obligations for balance-of-payments purposes, with no conversion ratios or repatriation deadlines.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility. Luxembourg-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) authorized by the CSSF under PSD2, or EU/EEA EMIs passing into Luxembourg under the freedom-of-services passport, can be used for operational collection and disbursement rails. They are not viable substitutes for full credit institutions when the SARL must hold capital escrow balances, issue guarantees, or establish complex trade-finance structures. Offshore EMIs without EU/EEA licensing face legal prohibition from providing payment services in Luxembourg unless properly passported, and will present significant AML/KYC and operational risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not mandate a single physical-meeting rule for corporate account opening. Most tier-1 banks permit remote onboarding using qualified video identification and advanced electronic signatures under CSSF AML circulars; however, in practice, banks frequently require at least one physical appearance by an authorized director or a professional intermediary (lawyer, notary, or fiduciary) for accounts with non-EEA shareholders or complex holding chains. For the LU_SARL which is directly owned by non-resident investors, institutional-recommended onboarding is: initial remote documentary submission, followed by either a physical meeting in Luxembourg or a bank-approved video interview with notarized powers of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or ultimate shareholder located in a jurisdiction classified as high-risk or non-cooperative by FATF, EU, or CSSF.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled corporate registry extracts, registered joint-venture or shareholder agreements, UBO registry transcript from the Luxembourg Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), independent source-of-wealth report prepared by a regulated fiduciary, and sanction-screening clearance from a recognized screening provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PropTech SaaS platform processing rental payments on behalf of third-party landlords, creating perceived third-party payment flows or unlicensed payment-service risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited operational agreements with landlords and tenants, a detailed description of the platform flow ensuring no legal reception of client funds, an external legal opinion under PSD2 classifying the model as non-payment-service activity, a written AML/CFT risk assessment, and current CSSF registration confirmation if any exemptions apply.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex cross-shareholding or multi-tier corporate structure obscuring the economic substance of the SARL.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete organizational chart, chain-of-title documents, constitutional documents of each intermediate holding entity, audited financial statements for the prior two years, evidence of substance (local registered office, Luxembourg resident directors, physical operational activity), and declaration confirming the absence of nominee-shareholder arrangements without proper disclosure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: THREAT OF REVERSE KYC RED FLAG: High-volume Euro inbound transfers from many international SaaS customers with limited supporting documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer contracting framework, contractual terms and conditions, transaction monitoring policy, Know-Your-Business screening for merchant customers, platform usage reports, and a wallet/treasury policy limiting aggregated customer funds in the operating account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant injection of share capital, shareholder loans, or intercompany contributions is routed via SWIFT MT103 over TARGET2 for EUR-denominated wires. The transfer should reference the Luxembourg balance-of-payments statistical purpose code (e.g., Code 'FDI' / Capital-in-kind identifier) and the SARL's standing client reference. Verification protocols require matching the received amount to the shareholders' recorded commitment in the statutory accounts, the CSSF UBO declaration, and the capital call documentation. Amounts exceeding EUR 50,000 require standard AML identification and may prompt Article 4 law requests; always execute the capital injection as a single clear-correspondent EUR transfer without intermediary currency conversion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for SaaS procurement, cloud-hosting fees, technology royalties, and subcontracted services are settled via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for euro-area counterparts. For non-euro trade settlement, SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers are used. If the underlying commercial contract necessitates documentary instrument protection, the disbursement rail may be a Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) with an advising and confirming Luxembourg bank, or a documentary collection (URC522) using a bill of exchange. All outgoing payments must map to appropriate tax and balance-of-payments statistics codes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts on EUR/USD or EUR/GBP negotiated with the relationship bank under an ISDA/CSA collateral arrangement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies without deliverable local liquidity, subject to bank credit limits
Cross-currency swaps between EUR and USD for long-term hedges of intercompany loans and shareholder advances
FX options (call and put) purchased to hedge downside risk while retaining upside exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet, profit and loss account, and notes) filed with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the end of the financial year (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties up to EUR 5,000; subsequent failures may trigger administrative strike-off or court-imposed fines up to EUR 25,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) – Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of initial RBE registration; continuous update within 30 days of any change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Daily fines of EUR 25 up to EUR 5,000 for late confirmation; intentional false declarations may incur penalties up to EUR 1,000,000 and imprisonment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax (CIT) and municipal business tax (MBT) annual return (Form 100 and MBT form)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing by 31 May of the following year; extended to 31 December if filed by a registered tax advisor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file: fines of EUR 100–2,500; tax assessment may be estimated administratively; interest on late payments at 0.6% per month.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL is exempt from mandatory audit if it does not exceed two of the three thresholds on two consecutive balance sheet dates: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average employees 50. Exceeding any two requires a certified statutory audit by an approved réviseur d'entreprises.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Accounting Law of 17 July 2008, implementing the EU Accounting Directive) is mandatory; IFRS may be voluntarily adopted in accordance with the law for unlisted entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, within 30 days of the RBE registration anniversary, the SARL must confirm the accuracy of the beneficial ownership details. Share transfers require an immediate amendment file to the RBE within 30 days of the transaction, detailing the new beneficial ownership percentages and identity of the transferee.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Luxembourg City aggregate headline rate 24.94% for FY2024/2025: CIT 17% + solidarity surcharge 7% on CIT (1.19 pts) + municipal business tax 6.75%; standalone CIT plus surcharge = 18.19%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Nexus-compliant 80% IP income deduction on qualifying PropTech/software IP: effective rate ~4.99% (24.94% x 20%); 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains; R&D investment tax credit; 30% EBITDA interest limitation cap as deduction ceiling (ATAD); municipal business tax deductible for CIT.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory time bar for commercial enterprises)
